reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    State: Texas
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: Is an officer of the court an individual empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?

    We model "writ of eviction" as the Texas "writ of possession" in an eviction suit (TX Prop  24.0061).
*/

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Basic helpers (pure, deterministic where used)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% integer_days_between(+FromDay, +ToDay, -DeltaDays)
integer_days_between(From, To, Delta) :-
    integer(From),
    integer(To),
    Delta is To - From.

% at_least_days_after(+FromDay, +ToDay, +MinDays)
at_least_days_after(From, To, MinDays) :-
    integer_days_between(From, To, Delta),
    Delta >= MinDays.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Statute encoding: TX Prop  24.0061 (2021) - Writ of Possession
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

/*
  TX Prop  24.0061(a):
  A landlord who prevails in an eviction suit is entitled to:
    - a judgment for possession, and
    - a writ of possession.
*/
statute_tx_24_0061_entitled_to_judgment_and_writ(Landlord, EvictionSuit) :-
    eviction_suit(EvictionSuit),
    landlord(Landlord),
    landlord_prevails_in_suit(Landlord, EvictionSuit).

/*
  TX Prop  24.0061(b):
  A writ of possession may not be issued before the 6th day after judgment
  unless:
    - a possession bond has been filed and approved, and
    - judgment for possession is thereafter granted by default.
*/
statute_tx_24_0061_writ_issuance_allowed(JudgmentDay, IssueDay, no_bond_no_default) :-
    integer(JudgmentDay),
    integer(IssueDay),
    at_least_days_after(JudgmentDay, IssueDay, 6),
    !.
statute_tx_24_0061_writ_issuance_allowed(_JudgmentDay, _IssueDay, bond_and_default_exception) :-
    possession_bond_filed_and_approved,
    default_judgment_for_possession_granted,
    !.

/*
  TX Prop  24.0061(d):
  The writ shall order the "officer executing the writ" to perform duties.
  (We encode the existence of an executing officer and some core duties.)
*/
statute_tx_24_0061_writ_orders_officer_to_post_warning_and_execute(Officer) :-
    statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer),
    !.

% Core duty: warning must specify execution on/after a date/time not sooner than 24 hours after posting.
% We model time in hours as integers for simplicity.
statute_tx_24_0061_warning_timing_ok(WarningPostedHour, EarliestExecutionHour) :-
    integer(WarningPostedHour),
    integer(EarliestExecutionHour),
    Delta is EarliestExecutionHour - WarningPostedHour,
    Delta >= 24.

% Core execution duties (summarized):
statute_tx_24_0061_execution_duty_deliver_possession_to_landlord(Officer) :-
    statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer),
    !.
statute_tx_24_0061_execution_duty_remove_occupants_if_noncompliant(Officer) :-
    statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer),
    !.
statute_tx_24_0061_execution_duty_supervise_property_removal(Officer) :-
    statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer),
    !.

/*
  TX Prop  24.0061(h):
  "A sheriff or constable may use reasonable force in executing a writ under this section."

  We treat this as the statute's explicit identification of who is empowered to execute
  the eviction writ (writ of possession) under this section: sheriffs and constables.

  Deterministic: succeeds iff Officer is a sheriff or constable.
*/
statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer) :-
    person(Officer),
    person_role(Officer, sheriff),
    !.
statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Officer) :-
    person(Officer),
    person_role(Officer, constable),
    !.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Scenario encoding (facts) + scenario_statement/0
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% Metadata
state(texas).
focus_year(2021).

/* Scenario: an "officer of the court" (not specified as sheriff/constable) */
person(alex).
person_role(alex, officer_of_the_court).

% For completeness of the statute model (not essential to the question):
landlord(l1).
eviction_suit(s1).
landlord_prevails_in_suit(l1, s1).

% No bond/default facts asserted in this scenario:
% possession_bond_filed_and_approved.
% default_judgment_for_possession_granted.

% scenario_statement/0 succeeds when the factual statement being tested is present.
% Here: we have an "officer of the court" individual we are asking about.
scenario_statement :-
    person(alex),
    person_role(alex, officer_of_the_court).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Legal issue / reasoning: "empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction"
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% We treat "writ of eviction" as the writ of possession in an eviction suit under TX Prop  24.0061.
legal_empowered_by_law_to_execute_eviction_writ(Person) :-
    statute_tx_24_0061_officer_authorized_to_execute_writ(Person),
    !.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Answer predicate
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_empowered_by_law_to_execute_eviction_writ(alex),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    \+ legal_empowered_by_law_to_execute_eviction_writ(alex),
    !.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Main entrypoint (required)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Is an officer of the court an individual empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?
